dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:8901.text: A general term for creatures. Formed from two 虫. All characters in this group are formed from 䖵. Read like 昆.

shuowen:8902.text: That which bears silk. Formed from 䖵, with 朁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8903.text: The flying creature into which a silkworm transforms. Formed from 䖵, with 我 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8904.text: A jumping creature that bites people. Formed from 䖵, with 㕚 indicating the sound. 㕚 is ancient 爪.

shuowen:8905.text: A creature that bites people. Formed from 䖵, with 卂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8906.text: A locust. Formed from 䖵, with 夂 indicating the sound. 夂 is ancient-script 終.

shuowen:8907.text: A creature. Formed from 䖵, with abbreviated 展 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8908.text: A small cicada. Formed from 䖵, with 𢧵 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8909.text: 蠿蟊, the web-making creature called 蛛蟊. Formed from 䖵, with 𢇍 indicating the sound. 𢇍 is ancient 絕.

shuowen:8910.text: The creature called 蠿蟊. Formed from 䖵, with 矛 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8911.text: A creature. Formed from 䖵, with 寍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8912.text: The creature called 𧓉𧕐. Formed from 䖵, with 曹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8913.text: The creature called 螻蛄. Formed from 䖵, with 舝 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8914.text: The creature called 𧓎蛸. Formed from 䖵, with 卑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8915.text: A flying creature that stings people. Formed from 䖵, with 逢 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8916.text: The sweet substance of bees. Alternatively, the young of 螟. Formed from 䖵, with 鼏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8917.text: The creature called 螶𧐑. Formed from 䖵, with 巨 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8918.text: A flying creature that bites people. Formed from 䖵, with 民 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8919.text: A flying creature that bites people. Formed from 䖵, with 亡 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8920.text: A creature inside wood. Formed from 䖵, with 橐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8921.text: A creature eating into wood. Formed from 䖵, with 彖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8922.text: A many-footed creature. Formed from 䖵, with 求 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8923.text: The creature called 蚍𧖚. Formed from 䖵, with 㯱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8924.text: A creature eating. Formed from 䖵, with 雋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8925.text: Creatures moving. Formed from 䖵, with 春 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8926.text: Those with feet are called 蟲; those without feet, 豸. Formed from three 虫. All characters in this group are formed from 蟲.

shuowen:8927.text: A creature that eats grass roots. Formed from 蟲, depicting its shape. It appears when officials act brazenly and take the people's wealth.

shuowen:8928.text: 蚍蜉, a large ant. Formed from 蟲, with 𣬈 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8929.text: A mosquito. Formed from 蟲, with 𨳌 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8930.text: A foul-smelling creature, called 負蠜. Formed from 蟲, with 非 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8931.text: Creatures in the abdomen. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: 'Creatures in a vessel make 蠱'; 'It arises from darkness and licentiousness.' The ghosts of those who die impaled or violently also become 蠱, apparently. Formed from 蟲 and 皿. 皿 is a vessel for use.

shuowen:8932.text: The eight winds: east, 明庶; southeast, 清明; south, 景; southwest, 涼; west, 閶闔; northwest, 不周; north, 廣莫; northeast, 融. Wind moves and creatures are born; hence creatures transform in eight days. Formed from 虫, with 凡 indicating the sound. All characters in this group are formed from 風.

shuowen:8933.text: The north wind is called 𩘁. Formed from 風, with abbreviated 涼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8934.text: A slight wind. Formed from 風, with 朮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8935.text: A rising whirlwind. Formed from 風, with 猋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8936.text: A revolving wind. Formed from 風, with 㶾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8937.text: A soaring wind. Formed from 風, with 立 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8938.text: A high wind. Formed from 風, with 翏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8939.text: A swift wind. Formed from 風 and 忽; 忽 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:8940.text: A great wind. Formed from 風, with 胃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8941.text: A great wind. Formed from 風, with 日 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8942.text: What the wind lifts and sends flying. Formed from 風, with 昜 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8943.text: Wind and rain sudden and violent. Formed from 風, with 利 indicating the sound. Read like 栗.

shuowen:8944.text: A fierce wind. Formed from 風, with 𠛱 indicating the sound. Read like 𠛱.

shuowen:8945.text: A cool breeze. Formed from 風, with 思 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8946.text: The condition expressed by 颼飂, apparently wind blowing. Formed from 風, with 叜 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8947.text: Wind blowing and waves moving. Formed from 風, with 占 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8948.text: A snake. Formed from 虫 elongated, depicting a winding body and hanging tail. In high antiquity people lived among grasses and feared snakes, so they asked one another: 'No snakes?' All characters in this group are formed from 它.

shuowen:8949.text: Old or enduring. Bones outside and flesh within. Formed from 它, since a turtle's head and snake's head are alike. By the nature of heaven and earth, broad-shouldered creatures have no males; turtles and soft-shelled turtles take snakes as males. It depicts feet, shell, and tail. All characters in this group are formed from 龜.

shuowen:8950.text: A turtle's name. Formed from 龜, with 夂 indicating the sound. 夂 is ancient-script 終.

shuowen:8951.text: The edge of a turtle shell. Formed from 龜, with 冄 indicating the sound. The Son of Heaven's large shell is one chi and two cun; a feudal lord's, one chi; a great officer's, eight cun; a gentleman's, six cun.

shuowen:8952.text: A frog, 鼃黽. Formed from 它; a pictograph. The head of 𪓑 is the same as that of 它. All characters in the 𪓑 group are formed from 𪓑.

shuowen:8953.text: A shelled creature. Formed from 𪓑, with 敝 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8954.text: A large soft-shelled turtle. Formed from 𪓑, with 元 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8955.text: A frog, 蝦蟇. Formed from 𪓑, with 圭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8956.text: 圥鼀 is the creature called 詹諸. Its call sounds 詹諸, its skin is bumpy, and its movement hopping. Formed from 黽 and 圥; 圥 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:8957.text: 𪓰𪓿, the creature called 詹諸. The Odes says: 'Obtain this 𪓰𪓿,' referring to its movement. Formed from 黽, with 爾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8958.text: An aquatic creature resembling a lizard, long and large. Formed from 黽, with 單 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8959.text: An aquatic creature eaten by the 薉 and 貉 peoples. Formed from 黽, with 奚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8960.text: A kind of 𪓷, with two horns on its head, found in 遼東. Formed from 黽, with 句 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8961.text: The buzzing blue-green fly, a creature with a large belly. Formed from 黽 and 虫.

shuowen:8962.text: 䵹鼄 is the creature called 蟊. Formed from 黽, with abbreviated 𥏼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8963.text: The creature called 䵹鼄. Formed from 黽, with 朱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8964.text: The creature called 匽鼂. Read like 朝. Yang Xiong says 匽鼂 is a creature's name. Du Lin takes it as morning, which is wrong. Formed from 黽 and 旦.

shuowen:8965.text: A great sea turtle. Formed from 黽, with 敖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8966.text: All creatures without milk are born from eggs. A pictograph. All characters in this group are formed from 卵.

shuowen:8967.text: An egg failing to hatch. Formed from 卵, with 段 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8968.text: The number of earth. Formed from a pair of 一. All characters in this group are formed from 二.

shuowen:8969.text: Quick and swift. Formed from 人, 口, 又, and 二. 二 is heaven and earth.

shuowen:8970.text: Constant. Formed from 心 and 舟 between the upper and lower strokes of 二. The heart moves by means of a boat: this is constancy, apparently.

shuowen:8971.text: To seek throughout. Formed from 二 and 囘. 囘 is ancient-script 回, depicting circling all around. Above and below are the things sought.

shuowen:8972.text: Thick or substantial. Formed from 二, with 竹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8973.text: To encompass altogether. Formed from 二, a pair, and 𠄎, an ancient form of 及.

shuowen:8974.text: That through which the earth brings forth things. 二 depicts below the earth and within it, with a thing emerging. All characters in this group are formed from 土.

shuowen:8975.text: When primal vapor first divided, the light, clear yang became heaven; the heavy, turbid yin became earth. It is where all things are arrayed. Formed from 土, with 也 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8976.text: Earth; a hexagram of the Changes. Formed from 土 and 申. Earth's position is at 申.

shuowen:8977.text: The lands encompassing the eight extremities. The Discourses of the States says: 'The Son of Heaven dwells in the lands of the nine regions.' Formed from 土, with 亥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8978.text: Habitable ground in the four directions. Formed from 土, with 奧 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8979.text: 堣夷 is in 陽谷, 冀州. On the day Beginning of Spring, the sun rises directly opposite it. Formed from 土, with 禺 indicating the sound. The Book of Documents says: 'Dwell at 堣夷.'

shuowen:8980.text: A place seventy li south of 朝歌. The Book of Zhou says: 'King Wu fought Zhou at the field of Mu.' Formed from 土, with 母 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8981.text: A slope. Formed from 土, with 皮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8982.text: Level ground. Formed from 土 and 平; 平 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:8983.text: Even throughout. Formed from 土 and 勻; 勻 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:8984.text: Soft soil. Formed from 土, with 襄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8985.text: Firm and impossible to pull out. Formed from 土, with 高 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8986.text: Hard, stony soil. Formed from 土, with 敫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8987.text: Hard soil. Formed from 土, with 盧 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8988.text: Red, hard soil. Formed from 土, with abbreviated 觲 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8989.text: Sticky earth. Formed from 土, with 直 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8990.text: Earth in clods. Formed from 土, with 圥 indicating the sound. Read like 逐. Another explanation gives 坴梁.

shuowen:8991.text: Earth. In Luoyang there is a 大𡍦 neighborhood. Formed from 土, with 軍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8992.text: A clod. Formed from 土, with 菐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8993.text: A clod. Formed from 土, with a bent enclosing stroke depicting its shape.

shuowen:8994.text: A clod. Formed from 土, with 畐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8995.text: To plant. Alternatively, to place within it. Formed from 土, with 㚇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8996.text: A ridge between rice plots. Formed from 土, with 朕 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8997.text: To put in order. Alternatively, shoveling earth is called 坺. The Odes says: 'King Wu then set to work.' Alternatively, the appearance of dust. Formed from 土, with 犮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8998.text: An opening in a pottery kiln. Formed from 土, with abbreviated 役 indicating the sound.

shuowen:8999.text: The beginning or base of a wall. Formed from 土, with 其 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9000.text: A wall. Formed from 土, with 亘 indicating the sound.
